subject: Pilot sizing & reserved-throughput checklist for BrightLane (post-demo)
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Carter Jenkins <carter.jenkins@brightlane.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing & reserved-throughput checklist for BrightLane (post-demo)

Hi Carter / Lena —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size the dedicated pilot and lock in reserved throughput that meets your SLOs. I tried to capture the items we discussed on latency/throughput/streaming so the pilot gives representative numbers.

Recap of BrightLane target SLOs (as discussed):
- API p95 latency (chat streaming): <= 120 ms for user-facing tokens (most requests are streaming).
- End-to-end request latency (first-token): <= 80 ms for 90% of requests.
- Sustained throughput: ~1,200 concurrent streams during peak (average token rate ~8 tps per stream).
- Burst concurrency tolerance: up to 2,500 concurrent streams for short bursts (~60s).

Questions / asks for sizing:
1) Confirm typical sequence lengths and average token generation per session (you noted ~600 tokens per session on average).
2) Confirm percent of requests that use streaming vs full-block generation (you said ~85% streaming).
3) Any special model variants (reranking or embeddings at high volume) we should include in pilot?

Initial Redwood recommendation (pilot baseline):
- Hardware shortlist: H100 80GB (primary), A100 80GB (fallback). H100 preferred for throughput + streaming concurrency.
- Pilot reserved throughput: target steady-state for pilot = capacity to handle 1,200 concurrent streaming sessions at average 8 tps (approx ~9.6k tokens/s). We recommend reserving enough GPUs to sustain ~12k tokens/s to give headroom.
- Pilot scale: start with 2x H100 nodes (load-tested) and validate. If observed token/s or p95 is higher, scale to 4x H100.

Deliverables we will share for the pilot kickoff:
- Baseline bench CSV: benchmark_results.csv (attached) — end-to-end p95, latency-to-first-token, tokens/s per GPU and resource utilization.
- Inference profile doc: ml-inference-profiles.pdf (attached) — how we configure kernel choices, KV cache, and streaming batch sizes per model.
- Mutual action plan: mutual-action-plan.docx (attached) — timeline, sign-offs, and success criteria.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the numbers above and attach a short sample traffic trace (or metrics export) so our SRE can replay realistic sequences.
- Internal: Jordan will propose an initial GPU shortlist and run a lightweight bench with your sample.
- We schedule a pilot kick-off the week of Oct 16 if everything checks out.

If that aligns, I’ll get Jordan to run the preliminary bench and share results by Oct 10.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Sofia —

Appreciate the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Average tokens per session is closer to 550 (range 300–1,200).
- Streaming %: yes ~85% streaming, 15% synchronous batched responses (semantic search / rerank).
- We do run a high-volume reranker at peak (~200 qps) that you should include in the pilot; it runs a smaller encoder model (embeddings + lightweight cross-attention).

Traffic trace: attaching a sanitized sample trace (ops@brightlane.ai will follow with the export).

Also: curious about the delta between H100 and A100 for streaming. If the pilot can start with A100s for cost reasons and we see we need H100 later, that could be acceptable.

Can Jordan include a quick comparison of p95 and tokens/s per GPU for both cards in the initial bench? That will help our infra team decide.

Thanks —
Carter
Carter Jenkins
Head of Platform, BrightLane

Subject: RE: Pilot sizing & reserved-throughput checklist for BrightLane (post-demo)

Hi all —

Thanks Carter — I’ll include the reranker profile in the bench. Quick notes on the H100 vs A100 comparison I’ll run (initial scope):
- Workloads: streaming chat (long KV cache lifetimes), synchronous rerank (batched 200 qps target), and embeddings microbench.
- Metrics: end-to-end p95 streaming (ms), first-token latency (ms), tokens/s per GPU at target utilization, memory headroom for KV cache, CPU network contention.
- Test plan: replay sanitized trace at real-time rates up to 1.2k concurrent streams and run burst tests to 2.5k for 60s windows.
- Pilot config: 2x nodes (H100 or A100) with contiguous CPU+NIC sizing; if p95 drift > 25% or tokens/s per GPU < 75% of expected, add 2 more nodes.

Preliminary hypothesis (what we expect to see):
- H100 will show ~20–30% higher tokens/s for streaming workloads at comparable p95 vs A100 due to improved kernel and memory throughput for large KV caches.
- A100 will be close on first-token latency but may need more replicas for sustained streaming concurrency.

I’ll run the bench this week once we have the traffic trace and will attach the CSV output and short summary.

-Ben, can you validate the perf harness and confirm the benchmark artifacts we’ll hand to BrightLane (CSV + brief README)?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot sizing & reserved-throughput checklist for BrightLane (post-demo)

Carter / team —

Bench run is complete (attached). Quick summary of results and recommended next steps:

Summary findings (from benchmark_results.csv):
- H100 (2 nodes) sustaining ~11.8k tokens/s with p95 streaming = 105 ms, first-token 72 ms, KV-cache hit ratio 94%.
- A100 (2 nodes) sustaining ~8.9k tokens/s with p95 streaming = 140 ms, first-token 78 ms, KV-cache hit ratio 92%.
- Reranker (batched 200 qps) performed similarly on both cards for raw throughput but A100 used ~18% more GPU memory headroom under mixed load.
- Under 60s burst to 2.5k concurrent streams: H100 p95 drift to ~140 ms; A100 drift to ~210 ms.

Recommendations:
1) Pilot reservation: provision 3x H100 nodes for the initial 30-day pilot. That targets sustained ~17k tokens/s and gives headroom for KV cache / rerank overhead.
2) If budget-constrained: start with 2x A100 with automatic fallback to burst pool (hosted) for overflow; but expect ~25% higher latency and additional replicas to hit concurrency targets.
3) Acceptance criteria for pilot success: sustained p95 <= 120 ms for streaming at 1.2k concurrent sessions and burst handling to 2.5k with p95 <= 200 ms.

Attachments: benchmark_results.csv, perf-readme.txt (brief how-to), and the mut-action plan updated with these numbers.

Let us know when you want the pilot contract (I can loop in CS/Contracts).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
